title: Interop playbook: SDK streaming + tool workflows (TS / Py / Go)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a practical interop playbook and reference implementations for SDK streaming + tool/function calling + structured output across TypeScript, Python, and Go. Deliverables: 1) stable interface patterns (async iterators / async generators / channel-based streams), 2) tool registry and invocation examples, 3) structured output schema patterns and migration guidance, 4) short samples for backpressure, resumption, and compatibility shims for older clients.
acceptance_criteria: TS/Py/Go reference clients implement the same high-level UX for: streaming tokens, streaming structured events, tool call lifecycle (init, call, result, error), and graceful resume after dropped connection
Examples include small end-to-end app e2e: prompt -> tool call (HTTP lookup simulated) -> structured JSON response validated by schema
Migration guide documents mapping from legacy streaming envelopes to new framed events and sample shim code for older SDK versions
PRs approved and merged: SDK changes + three language example repos; CI smoke tests passing on linux-amd64 and macos for TS builds
implementation_notes: Design choice: unify on event-framed stream where each frame has a 'type' field (token|tool_event|structured|checkpoint) and an id to correlate session and tool calls

TS pattern: async iterator that yields discriminated union types (TokenEvent | ToolEvent | StructuredEvent). Provide convenience 'collect' helper that reconstructs messages and rehydrates tool call futures.
Py pattern: async generator with pydantic models for schema validation. Add SessionState object for resumption tokens. Keep runtime dependency minimal (typing + pydantic optional).

Go pattern: channel-based stream with a StreamEvent interface and concrete structs. Provide helper that spawns a goroutine to decode envelopes and preserves order while exposing a typed API for tool results. Avoid heavy reflection; use json.RawMessage where needed.

Compatibility shim: provide a small adapter in each language that maps old newline-delimited token streams to framed events by injecting 'token' frames. This reduces immediate client breakage for customers on older SDK versions.

Backpressure: recommend SDK-level buffer of configurable size with drop-policy 'block|drop-latest|drop-oldest' and default to 'block' for developer ergonomics. Include example showing blocking behavior in Go with context cancellation.
Resumption: sessions will emit periodic 'checkpoint' frames containing a compact resume token (opaque base64). Documentation shows how to store/attach a resume_token in subsequent connections.

2025-02-18: Early prototype for TS async iterator landed in branch feature/sdk-playbook-ts. Rafael: initial feedback - iterator ergonomics good, need clearer error propagation for tool failures.
2025-02-21: Python prototype demonstrates pydantic-based StructuredEvent validation. Maya: prefer optional validation toggle to avoid pulling pydantic for minimal installs.
2025-02-25: Go implementation spike shows channel pattern but highlighted complexity around ordered tool call results when concurrency >1. Proposed helper 'OrderedFanIn' to preserve ordering.
2025-02-28: Design review - @Anika Patel requested explicit examples for migrators from legacy NDJSON streams. Assigned follow-up task to create 'legacy-shim' module per language.
2025-03-03: Rafael: merged TS convenience helpers after address comments. Next: finalize Go concurrency helper and add test coverage for resume tokens.
design_doc: Playbook: event-framing.md (in repo) - explains frame types and examples
risks: Customers using raw NDJSON streaming will need to adopt shims; risk of bugs in shim mapping causing message reordering or dropped tool events
Adding resume tokens increases surface area for security review (tokens must be opaque and short-lived).
Introducing optional pydantic dependency may complicate packaging for minimal installs; solution: optional-extra 'validation' with clear docs.
qa_plan: Add e2e smoke: start server with deterministic tool responder, stream a prompt, simulate mid-stream disconnect, resume with checkpoint token, assert final structured output matches expected
Language SDK unit tests for framing/deframing, backpressure policies, and shim behavior
Manual run-through by DX with small sample apps on Hosted and Dedicated to validate fallbacks and resume semantics
